2011_025_071211regmtg.paragraph: Board agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, July 12, 2011, held at 7:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The dominant action item is the second phase of a district-wide laptop refresh, recommended for award across six vendors for a total of $1,804,916.25 and charged as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. The packet also carries three administrative appointments effective July 13, 2011, MHSAA membership for August 1, 2011 through July 31, 2012, an annual summer tax resolution, and a resolution calling the regular school election for November 8, 2011.

**Meeting**
Regular Meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, Tuesday, July 12, 2011, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000). Meetings are cable cast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Consent Agenda (Item 5)**
Minutes of the June 7, 2011 Board of Education Meeting, the June 14, 2011 Board Workshop, and the June 14, 2011 Special Board Meeting.

June 7, 2011 regular meeting at Athens High School: called to order by President Philippart at 7:05 p.m.; Board members Edmunds, Hauff, Fleming, Malven, Miletti and Underwood present, with Superintendent Fowler, administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Goss, Fulcher, Gebbie, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter and Witt, and approximately 140 members of the audience. A long recognition block honored All-State winter athletes and 66 senior scholar athletes with a 3.5 cumulative grade point average. Motions: 11-055 added TESPA Contract Ratification to the agenda; 11-056 ratified the tentative agreement reached May 25, 2011 with the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA for July 1, 2010 through June 30, 2012; 11-057 authorized the food service contract renewal with Sodexo Management, Inc. for 2011/2012 subject to Michigan Department of Education approval; 11-058 set the budget public hearing for June 21, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road; 11-059 moved to closed session on negotiations. All votes were 7-0. Closed session began at 9:27 p.m., the meeting reconvened at 9:45 p.m., and adjourned at 11:22 p.m.

June 14, 2011 Workshop: 6:00 p.m., Fleming absent, five additional community members; topics were enrollment/staffing, the 2011/2012 budget update including the final appropriation amendment for 2010/2011, and a special education programming overview. Adjourned 10:32 p.m.

June 14, 2011 Special Meeting: 11-060 issued Stephanie Acord a two-year probationary administrative contract as Principal, Morse Elementary School, effective July 1, 2011; 11-061 ratified the TESA tentative agreement reached June 9, 2011 for July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2013; 11-062 authorized a closed session. Votes 6-0, Fleming absent. Six residents spoke, several on the Troy Public Library millage on the August 2nd ballot.

**Personnel (Item 6)**
| Item | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| 6.A | Jennifer Doptis, 1.0 FTE English Teacher, Troy High School, probationary contract for 2011-2012 |
| 6.B | Anthony Morse, Assistant Principal, Boulan Park Middle School, effective July 13, 2011 |
| 6.C | David Pass, Elementary Principal, effective July 13, 2011 |
| 6.D | Matt Jansen, Elementary Principal, effective July 13, 2011 |

**Curriculum (Item 7)**
MHSAA membership resolution enrolling the district's six (6) secondary schools for August 1, 2011 through July 31, 2012. Appointment of Katie Andrea to an additional three-year term and Cindy Desmon to a three-year term on the Oakland Schools' Special Education Parent Advisory Committee, succeeding outgoing representative Lisa Matzenbach. Second reading and consideration of Code of Student Conduct revisions, first read June 21, 2011.

**Business (Item 8) - Laptop Refresh**
| Vendor | Cooperative Bid | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| InaComp TSG (HP) | REMC | $943,014.64 |
| Apple | REMC-Apple Direct | $534,628.72 |
| Merit | Merit Cooperative Bid | $155,652.24 |
| Netech (Cisco) | MICTA | $139,233.65 |
| JAMF Software | Quote | $8,000.00 |
| CDWg | AEPA | $24,387.00 |
| Total | | $1,804,916.25 |

**Other (Item 10)**
Annual summer tax resolution continuing collection of one-half of school property taxes, including debt service, and a resolution calling the regular school election of November 8, 2011 to elect three (3) members to six (6) year terms ending December 31, 2017.
2011_025_071211regmtg.verbose:
Agenda packet for the Regular Meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, Tuesday, July 12, 2011, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000. Board meetings are cable cast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

CONSENT AGENDA - JUNE 7, 2011 MINUTES
The June 7, 2011 regular meeting was held at Athens High School and called to order by President Philippart at 7:05 p.m., with Board members Edmunds, Hauff, Fleming, Malven, Miletti and Underwood; Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Goss, Fulcher, Gebbie, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter and Witt; and approximately 140 members of the audience. Mike Jolly and the Board recognized All-State winter athletes including Merna Abdou, Katie Cox, Jacob Duzey, Karen Hug, Miles McDonald, Annie Xiao and Carlie Zitkus, plus 66 senior scholar athletes who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average. Further recognitions covered Destination ImagiNation teams from Leonard (first in the State Finals against 39 teams) and Larson (second against 35 teams), 14 Michigan Green Schools, sixteen Midwest Talent Search honorees at Northwestern University among the top 21,000 nationally, sixteen students with a perfect score of 25 on the ACT Explore, Dhruv Medarametia's second place in National MATHCOUNTS, Julia Alaimo of Smith winning the Ford Freedom Essay Contest and a $5,000 savings bond, seven Athens students who won the Michigan Fed Challenge and placed second nationally, 42 National Merit semifinalists with eight finalists, more than 350 Advanced Placement Scholars, nine DECA students with advisor Heide Rosenberg, Intel science fair finalists Xiao Zhu, Lawrence Kim and Goutham Kapa, and Annie Xiao, first in the Michigan Brain Bee, fourth nationally, and tenth out of 4,538 in the National Biology Competition.

Motions: 11-055 (Malven/Fleming) added Item 5.A, TESPA Contract Ratification, 7-0. 11-056 (Hauff/Edmunds) ratified the tentative agreement reached May 25, 2011 with the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA) for July 1, 2010 through June 30, 2012, 7-0. 11-057 (Fleming/Miletti) authorized renewal of the food service contract with Sodexo Management, Inc. for 2011/2012 once Michigan Department of Education approval is received, 7-0. 11-058 set a public hearing on the proposed 2011/2012 budget for June 21, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, with notice published at least six (6) days beforehand carrying the required 11-point bold faced millage statement, 7-0. Bruce Bloomingdale commended Superintendent Fowler, Mr. Witt and the negotiating teams. 11-059 (Malven/Hauff) authorized a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), 7-0 on roll call; closed session began 9:27 p.m., the meeting reconvened 9:45 p.m., and adjourned 11:22 p.m. Paula Fleming, Secretary.

JUNE 14, 2011 WORKSHOP AND SPECIAL MEETING
The workshop convened at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building with Philippart, Edmunds, Hauff, Malven, Miletti and Underwood, Fleming absent, Superintendent Fowler and administrators Keeling, Machesky, Jagels, Hannon, Rajter and Witt, plus five community members; topics were enrollment/staffing, the 2011/2012 budget update including the final appropriation amendment for 2010/2011, and special education programming. Adjourned 10:32 p.m. The special meeting convened at 7:00 p.m.; Item 6.B, TESA Contract Ratification, was added. Resolution 11-060 (Hauff/Edmunds) issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Stephanie Acord as Principal, Morse Elementary School, effective July 1, 2011, 6-0. Resolution 11-061 (Miletti/Malven) ratified the tentative agreement reached June 9, 2011 with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA (TESA) for July 1, 2011 through June 30, 2013, 6-0. Residents Marti Steiner, Jieun Park, Kathy Welch, Edna Abrahim, Jennifer Hilzinger and Bruce Bloomingdale addressed the Board, most urging support for the Troy Public Library millage on the August 2nd ballot. Resolution 11-062 (Underwood/Edmunds) authorized a closed session on negotiations, 6-0; the closed-session and adjournment times are left blank in the minutes.

PERSONNEL
6.A recommends a probationary contract for Jennifer Doptis, 1.0 FTE English Teacher, Troy High School, for 2011-2012. 6.B recommends Anthony Morse as Assistant Principal, Boulan Park Middle School, effective July 13, 2011; he came from Madison District Public Schools, where he began as a high school social studies teacher in August of 2002 and became Principal of Wilkinson Middle School in 2008, and holds degrees from Central Michigan University (1997), Marygrove College (2004) and Oakland University (2009). 6.C recommends David Pass as Elementary Principal effective July 13, 2011; he came from the Avondale School District, where he was Principal at R. Grant Graham Elementary School for six years and Assistant Principal at Avondale Middle School for two years, following eight years as a Waterford School District middle school math teacher, with a Bachelor of Science in Elementary Education (1995) and a Master of Education (August 2003). 6.D recommends Matt Jansen as Elementary Principal effective July 13, 2011; he came to Troy in 1998 as a third grade teacher at Wass Elementary School, taught fourth grade for three years, became a fifth grade teacher at Wass in 2002, completed the Troy Academy for Learning Leaders (TALL) program, and coordinated Wass's Continuous Improvement Team for four years, holding degrees from Saginaw Valley State University (1998 and 2005). Each administrative appointment is a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure.

CURRICULUM
7.A adopts the Michigan High School Athletic Association membership resolution enrolling the six (6) secondary schools under the Board's direction, City of Troy, County of Oakland, for August 1, 2011 through July 31, 2012, accepting the MHSAA Constitution, By-laws and HANDBOOK as governing code; the MHSAA is at 1661 Ramblewood Drive, East Lansing, MI 48823, (517) 332-5046. 7.B appoints Mrs. Katie Andrea to an additional three-year term and Mrs. Cindy Desmon to a three-year term on the Oakland Schools' Special Education Parent Advisory Committee, with Mrs. Lisa Matzenbach's term ending. 7.C is the second reading of Code of Student Conduct revisions, first read at the June 21, 2011 meeting.

BUSINESS - DISTRICT LAPTOP REFRESH
A July 7, 2011 memorandum from Merri Lynn Colligan, Director of Technology (Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, 248/823-5090) to Dr. Fowler notes that the 2004 Bond issue planned two refresh cycles, the first deploying 1500 laptops in 2007, and that the useful life of a laptop is 4 years. During 2010-11 staff piloted the iPad Challenge, presented at the April Board meeting; the Troy Cloud will extend the life of the 2007 laptops at the middle and high schools. Pricing was drawn from REMC, MICTA, AEPA and Merit cooperative bids under the Board Purchasing Policy. The three-tier plan provides per elementary 30 iPads and 30 HP 6460b laptops; per middle school 30 iPads, 60 laptops and 30 Troy Cloud licenses; per high school 30 iPads, 60 laptops and 60 licenses; and 60 iPads with 160 laptops for Services/Administrative. The worksheet lists March 2011 enrollment and current laptops by building, among them Barnard 510/56, Costello 330/56, Schroeder 507/56, Baker 706/90, Smith 729/90, Athens 1783/136, Troy High 2075/148 and Niles 156/72; district totals are 11990 enrollment, 1551 current laptops, a current ratio of 7.73, 660 iPads, 1000 HP laptops, 300 VMware cloud seats, 1960 total new devices and a new ratio of 6.12. The budget planning sheet shows warranty of $538.00 and $841.34, device cost of $355,080.00 and $841,340.00, cart cost of $99,838.00 and $90,674.64, case and accessories of $30,415.80 and $11,000.00, apps and licensing of $66,240.00, server hardware of $7,441.92 and $139,233.65, server licensing of $8,000.00 and $155,652.24, and column totals of $567,015.72, $943,014.64 and $294,885.89 against a grand total of $1,804,916.25.

The resolution awards the bid as InaComp TSG (HP) $943,014.64 (REMC), Apple $534,628.72 (REMC-Apple Direct), Merit $155,652.24 (Merit Cooperative Bid), Netech (Cisco) $139,233.65 (MICTA), JAMF Software $8,000.00 and CDWg $24,387.00 (AEPA), totaling $1,804,916.25, approved as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund and described as a Bond Fund expenditure. Apple quote W71707515, dated 07-JUL-2011 and valid until 22-JUL-2011 from Jason Lewandowski, 1 Infinite Loop, Cupertino, CA 95014, lists 66 iPad 2 16GB Wi-Fi ten-packs with AppleCare at $5,380.00 for $355,080.00, 40 Bretford PowerSync carts at $2,495.95 for $99,838.00, 40 Apple TVs for $3,801.60, 60 volume vouchers at $960.00 for $57,600.00, four MacBook Pro 15-inch Core i7 units at $1,631.04 and two professional development days for $8,640.00, an Edu List Price Total of $542,110.00 less a $7,481.28 discount for $534,628.72. Hewlett-Packard quote 6709696-3, July 06, 2011, from Jamila Mamuya under contract MI - REMC (WSCA/NASPO) (HP-WSCA-09), Big Deal Number 86842614, covers 1000 HP ProBook 6460b notebooks (Intel Core i5-2410M 2.30GHz, 4 GB DDR3, 250 GB drive, Windows 7 Professional 32) at $741.34 for $741,340.00, 1000 five-year service plans at $100.00 for $100,000.00, 160 cases at $35.00 for $5,600.00, 56 charging carts at $1,619.19 for $90,674.64 and 40 docking stations at $135.00 for $5,400.00, totaling $943,014.64, with an optional 36-month lease at as little as $29,280.60 per month. CDW Government quote CFMZ820, account 5092865, dated 7/6/2011 and billed to Lois Hurdle at 4420 Livernois Rd, covers 660 Speck PixelSkin HD wraps at $36.95 for $24,387.00 under AEPA Technology Catalog 10-0045. JAMF Software quote Q-05796, created 7/5/2011, lists 1,000 Casper Suite for iOS licenses at $0.00 and 1,000 Casper Suite for iOS ASA at $8.00 for $8,000.00. The NETech Corporation Cisco UCS quote through MICTA, prepared by Scott Sutherland, totals $139,233.65, including a chassis bundle listed at $104,951.00 with a $47,227.95 unit cost, B250 M2 blades, Xeon X5675 3.06GHz processors and installation labor at $155.00 per hour covering VMware VDI for 500 clients. Merit Network quote 20110706-mls-01, dated 7/7/2011, lists six vSphere 4 Enterprise Plus licenses at $1,572.75, one vCenter Server 4 Standard at $2,247.75, one View 4 Premier 100-pack at $11,250.00, 65 View 4 Premier 10-packs at $1,125.00 for $73,125.00 and support lines of $8,452.98, $2,013.45, $6,550.26 and $42,576.30, totaling $155,652.24.

OTHER
10.A is the annual summer tax resolution: the Board intends to continue summer tax collections for the 2012-2013 fiscal year and will notify the City of Troy. Pursuant to 1976 P.A. 451, as amended, it invokes for 2011 the ongoing resolution imposing a summer levy of one-half of school property taxes, including debt service, beginning with 2012, directs that the resolution reach each city before January 1, 2012, and authorizes negotiation of collection expenses billable under MCLA 380.1612. 10.B calls the regular school election for Tuesday, November 8, 2011, at which three (3) members will be elected for six (6) year terms ending December 31, 2017. Both are certified as adopted at the regular meeting held July 12, 2011 with notice given under the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267, as amended.
